old: A Japanese 10 yen in bronze, dated Heisei 14 (2002), the fourteenth year of Emperor Akihito's reign. One side shows the Phoenix Hall of Byodoin temple in Uji, a thousand-year-old building whose rooftop phoenix statue also appeared on the 10,000 yen note. The other side frames a big 10 in a wreath of evergreen leaves. Japan has struck this design, nearly unchanged, since 1951, and it is still the 10 yen in everyday pockets today. The collection already holds two Showa-era strikes of the same design from 1982 and 1988; this is its first Heisei one.

old: This 1893 eight doubles coin from Guernsey is the oldest coin in this batch, struck during Queen Victoria's reign, though Guernsey's coins show no royal portrait and instead feature the island's shield with three lions from its Norman past and a sprig of leaves. The double was Guernsey's own Channel Islands currency counted eight to a British penny, so this large bronze piece matched the size of a penny, and Guernsey kept its doubles for a century before adopting the pound in full. It is the first coin from Guernsey in the collection. This piece shows plenty of age, with dark toning, smooth wear in places, and pale corrosion spots on the shield side.
